validation_case.given: a Bash script running with pipefail that checks content emitted by a potentially large command
validation_case.when: the check pipes the producer into a predicate that exits immediately after a match
validation_case.then: the check can fail on producer SIGPIPE even though the required content exists, so the producer output is captured and inspected without that early-exit pipeline

content.title: Under pipefail, capture large output before matching it
content.context: The tag workflow rejected a release whose target contained the required changelog heading. Under `set -o pipefail`, `git show <target>:CHANGELOG.md | grep -Fq ...` returned 141: grep matched early and exited, git show got SIGPIPE, and pipefail reported the whole check as failed.
content.guidance: Capture the producer's output once into a variable and match it in-shell (for example `[[ "$text" == *"needle"* ]]`), keeping the exact-content check. Do not use `producer | grep -q` as the validation result under pipefail.
content.why_it_works: The producer finishes writing before anything is matched, so no SIGPIPE can occur and the check's result depends only on the content.
content.when_to_apply: In Bash scripts or CI steps with `set -o pipefail` that check output of unbounded size, such as changelogs, logs or `git show` content.
content.when_not_to_apply: When the producer's output is guaranteed small, or when streaming is required because the output cannot be held in memory.
content.verification: vendor/bin/phpunit --filter ReleaseTagWorkflowTest (testNewTagAcceptsLargeTargetChangelogBeforeCreatingTheTag). The same construct also failed 5/5 in voku/agent-learning's release workflow at 75 KB (fixed in voku/agent-learning#197) and is fixed in agent-map#200 and agent-recall-compiler#280.
content.symptoms: A presence check reports content missing that is demonstrably present, typically only once the producer's output grows beyond the pipe buffer (about 64 KB); exit status 141 in traces.
content.root_cause: An early-exiting predicate (`grep -q`, `head`) closes the pipe while the producer is still writing; pipefail turns the producer's SIGPIPE into a failed pipeline.
